content_md:
Amara’s Law is that people overestimate a technology in the short term and underestimate it in the long term. 

I think AI is radically violating this pattern. What’s happening instead is that in the short term, people are wildly overestimating entirely fictional aspects and utterly wildly underestimating the very real nonfictional things. 

As for the long term nobody is actually estimating them at all due to the really bad premature ontologies.

Most people have no idea what’s about to hit them, though some have some sense of how hard it’s going to hit.

They’re using unimaginably lazy answers to the what, so even if they get the order of magnitude right on how hard, it doesn’t help.

“AGI” as an idea is an ontological high crime here.
